content.intro: In this lesson, you will study object initialization order with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you model valid object state and expose behavior without leaking implementation details. In this lesson, focus on field initializers and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A variable has a declared type and a scope. Initialize local variables before reading them; fields have defined default values, but relying on defaults can hide missing business logic. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect field initializers with instance initializer blocks before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API.
